topics.title: French supermarket fridges hit by hackers
topics.summary: A wave of cyberattacks disrupted supermarket refrigeration in France, raising questions about how everyday infrastructure is protected when connected systems go offline.
topics.discussionPrompt: It’s strange how quickly a fridge can become a national story. What everyday gadget would cause the biggest chaos if it suddenly stopped working everywhere?

topics.title: Thailand celebrates its vegetarian festival
topics.summary: Communities across Thailand are marking the annual vegetarian festival, a nine-day Taoist observance centered on meat-free food, rituals and renewal.
topics.discussionPrompt: Could you happily eat vegetarian for nine days if the food was amazing, or would you start bargaining for one very specific comfort meal?

topics.title: UN leadership vote remains unsettled
topics.summary: A new informal Security Council poll found that none of seven candidates for the next UN secretary-general has backing from all five permanent members.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a group has to choose one leader, is a compromise pick usually wise—or does it just make everyone mildly unhappy?

topics.title: Nature-protection funding gap draws attention
topics.summary: Fundraising for protecting oceans, forests and other important ecosystems remains well below the level advocates say is needed ahead of a UN biodiversity summit.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your neighborhood received a big nature budget, would you spend it on trees, water, wildlife habitat, parks, or something else?

topics.title: Study examines honeybees and wild pollinators
topics.summary: A new study says honeybees can crowd out wild pollinators while competing for pollen and nectar, adding nuance to the familiar image of bees as uncomplicated helpers.
topics.discussionPrompt: What’s a creature you assumed was purely helpful until you learned it can be a bit of a neighborhood bully?

topics.title: Drought may shrink England’s Halloween pumpkins
topics.summary: Growers expect smaller pumpkins this Halloween after drought conditions in England, a reminder that weather can reshape even the most ordinary seasonal traditions.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would a smaller pumpkin ruin your carving plans, or just challenge you to make the tiniest, funniest jack-o’-lantern possible?

topics.title: Brazil reports record-low Amazon deforestation
topics.summary: Brazil says Amazon deforestation has fallen to its lowest recorded level, while the country weighs major environmental choices ahead of an important vote.
topics.discussionPrompt: What kind of long-term project makes you most hopeful: restoring forests, cleaning rivers, renewable power, or protecting wildlife?

topics.title: NHS trusts question a patient-data platform
topics.summary: Many NHS trusts in England have declined a patient-data platform from Palantir, saying existing systems meet their needs and questioning the added value.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you switch to a shiny new app if your current one works fine, or do you need a truly irresistible feature first?

topics.title: World Cup friendlies fill the football calendar
topics.summary: England, Scotland and the United States are preparing for international friendlies as teams continue building toward the 2026 World Cup cycle.
topics.discussionPrompt: Are friendly matches a fun preview, or do they only become exciting once somebody invents a dramatic rivalry out of nowhere?

topics.title: Pope Leo set to leave hospital
topics.summary: The Vatican says Pope Leo will leave hospital four days after lung surgery and plans to deliver the traditional Sunday blessing from a St. Peter’s Square window.
topics.discussionPrompt: When someone bounces back after a tough week, what small celebration feels right: flowers, a favorite meal, a silly card, or quiet company?
